Subject: MAP + Acceptance Tests: Meridian pilot gating & cutover timeline

Claire — attaching our working Mutual Action Plan workbook (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx). This draft focuses on the evaluation success criteria and a compact set of exit gates so your team can validate production readiness in a 3-week pilot. High-level asks: please confirm the three acceptance tests in tab "Gates", and let me know any procurement evidence you need before we schedule the pilot cutover.

Key points in this draft:
- Success metrics: 95th pct latency < 450ms (hosted), end-to-end throughput 60 QPS for 4k token requests, embedding similarity recall >= 0.88 on your sample dataset.
- Exit gates: (1) Feature parity smoke tests pass, (2) Latency/cost within threshold over 48h window, (3) Data ingestion & retention workflow validated with audit logs.
- Acceptance tests: functional prompts (10 canonical prompts), load soak (48h, mixed qps), and trace-driven incident replay.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook)

Thanks — if the gates look reasonable I can turn this into a DocuSign-ready mutual action agreement and book a cutover slot next week.

— Ben

Ben — thanks for the workbook. A few clarifications from my side after skimming the "Gates" tab:

1) Latency target: 95th < 450ms looks ambitious for our longer clinical notes (avg 2.7k tokens). Can we show a short benchmark for 3k-token tail cases or add a separate tail gate (99th < 1.2s)?
2) Embeddings: we need a clear evaluation corpus. I attached a small sample (sent separately via SFTP) — for the MAP, can we specify the sample set and a scoring script we run together?
3) Audit logs: procurement needs evidence of retention policy and access controls (SOC2 test evidence is ideal). Is that the security-evidence PDF you referenced?

If you can update the MAP with a 'tail latency' gate and a concrete embeddings scoring step (we can run the script), procurement will move to the contract redline step. Also, can we schedule a 30-min runbook walkthrough the week of 5/15?

Thanks all — updated plan below (I've also updated the attached workbook and reuploaded to the Drive link):

Updated acceptance gates (short summary):
- Gate A (Functional): 10 canonical prompts pass with expected structured output (owner: Meridian product). Evidence: transcript + checker output.
- Gate B (Performance): 95th percentile < 450ms for <=4k tokens; Tail gate: 99th percentile < 1.2s for up to 3k-4k token cases. Evidence: 48h CSV metrics export.
- Gate C (Cost/Throughput): Average cost per 1k tokens within quoted bandwidth for 48h soak; load profile: 60 QPS sustained bursts up to 80 QPS for 15 minutes every 4 hours.
- Gate D (Security & Audit): Audit log extract + KMS bindings + security-evidence PDF.
- Gate E (Embedding recall): Shared scoring script + sample corpus; recall >= 0.88 on the sample.

Soak config (as a precise checklist):
1) Instance: rdw-dedicated-n1 (see Drive doc for exact AMI)
2) Concurrency: 60 rps steady state; burst 80 rps; mixed prompt lengths: 20% >2k tokens, 70% 1k-2k, 10% <1k
3) Batch size: dynamic up to 32 depending on token length
4) Monitoring: token-level latency traces, tail histograms, and cost per minute export

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: send the security-evidence PDF and add the sample log extract to the Drive folder by EOD Monday.
- Karthik: confirm the exact soak command-line and docker image tag we will use for the replicated run.
- Claire/Procurement: if these updates are acceptable, we can push the MAP to DocuSign and ask for a signature to lock the 3-week pilot window starting 5/22.

I've attached a revised MAP workbook and included the DocuSign link (below) — happy to jump on a 30-min runbook review on 5/16 per Claire's ask.

— Ben
